summary.headline: AVG Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose 29.98% to INR6.46 crore on revenue growth of 5.97% to INR132.48 crore; FY27 guidance 15-20% revenue growth.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose 5.97% YoY to INR132.48 crore, while PBT grew 24.42% to INR8.71 crore and PAT grew 29.98% to INR6.46 crore, with PBT and PAT margins expanding 98 bps and 89 bps. Management attributed the profit growth to fleet productivity, asset utilisation and cost discipline. The company completed a rights issue raising INR52.93 crore in Q1, secured a 100-vehicle Haldiram contract, and formed a JV (Carbonlite Logistics) with Baidyanath Group for LNG/EV transport. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15-20%, while noting Q1 is seasonally a softer quarter.

financial_highlights.metric: Rights issue proceeds received in Q1

financial_highlights.change: Record date September 18, 2026; AGM book closure Sept 19-25, 2026

segments.name: Dedicated / contract logistics
segments.commentary: Management cited dedicated vehicles, cold chain, reefer trucks and warehousing/factory management as higher-margin segments with less competition. Company is also doing customer warehouse operations.

segments.name: Liquid logistics
segments.commentary: Two tanker trains already purchased; a third to be taken on lease for about one year. Management said liquor freight rates are higher than normal goods, supporting better margins.

segments.name: Green transport (CNG/LNG/EV)
segments.commentary: Management expects lower operating costs versus diesel; LNG contract for 100 vehicles and 30 EV vehicles ordered, with a further 70 EV under discussion. JV Carbonlite Logistics expected to start operations from October 1, 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of approximately 15-20%: management split this as 7-8% from new business and 8-10% from existing customers via expansions and new contracts.
FY27 capex planned at about INR50-60 crore, supplemented by operating leases for additional fleet, particularly EVs.
Management expects margins to improve in FY27 as FY26 H2 capex assets contribute for a full year; depreciation will rise with the new assets.
Target to add about 200 vehicles by March 2027 (CNG 50-60, LNG 100 under Haldiram-related contract, EV 30 ordered plus 70 in discussion) — as stated by management.

Haldiram, Nagpur: 100 dedicated vehicles; 40 deployed as of August 21, 2026, remaining 60 expected within one to two months; customer has asked for another 100 vehicles by December 2026 (not yet contracted).
Operations of Carbonlite Logistics expected to start from October 1, 2026.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR62 crore; FY27 planned capex about INR50-60 crore, with some fleet to be taken on operating lease instead of purchase.
Fleet and warehousing footprint cited: more than 3,000 owned and hired vehicles, over 70 branches, more than 7.4 lakh sq ft warehousing.
Running-kilometre target: minimum 15-20% increase from about 1 lakh km per month, i.e. toward 1.2 lakh km per month; August reportedly saw the incremental growth begin.
Most FY26 capex was in the second half of FY26, so assets contribute for a full year in FY27.
demand_pricing: Haldiram contract indicates large FMCG customer demand; festive season (Ganesh Chaturthi to Diwali/Durga Puja) cited as demand driver.
Management said liquid logistics has strong demand and limited organised competition.
Customers are seeking cleaner transport; steel, metal, cement and FMCG companies cited as LNG/EV prospects.
Fuel escalation clauses in a significant portion of contracts help manage fuel price changes.
Management noted Q4 and Q3 are typically stronger quarters than Q1 and Q2 for volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue growth outlook after 6% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15-20% growth, with 7-8% from new business and 8-10% from existing customers, and said new fleet added in FY26 will contribute a full year in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What incremental revenue and PAT can the rights issue generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to attribute revenue or PAT to the rights issue alone; proceeds are mainly for working capital, with overall incremental revenue expected from new contracts and fleet utilisation. Depreciation will rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR60 crore of capex is planned (also referenced as INR50-60 crore), with leasing evaluated to balance the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Haldiram contract deployment on track and what is next?
qa_highlights.answer: 40 of 100 vehicles deployed on August 21, 2026; remaining 60 within one to two months. Customer has asked for another 100 vehicles by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Are liquid logistics tankers being bought or leased, and will margins improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Two tanker trains bought; one more on lease for about a year. Management expects margin improvement from FY26 capex and higher utilisation, and says liquid, EV and LNG segments carry higher margins.

qa_highlights.question: What does the in-house real-time tracking software do?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the GPS/dashcam platform gives customers real-time location and ETA, and is aimed at improving asset utilisation; target is 15-20% higher monthly running from about 1 lakh km.

risks_watch: Revenue growth of 6% in Q1 versus 15-20% full-year target; back-half weighting is required to meet guidance.
Depreciation will rise with new fleet; margin expansion depends on utilisation and running efficiency.
Capex and fleet targets are inconsistent in the call (INR50 crore vs INR60 crore; ~200 vehicles by March 2027) and need clarification.
Haldiram second 100-vehicle order is not yet contracted.
Carbonlite start-up on October 1, 2026 and leasing-based financing are dependent on third parties.
Net debt of about INR173 crore (March 2026) and the usage of rights-issue proceeds for working capital.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and margins, with repeated emphasis on disciplined capital deployment. Answers on rights-issue impact and the fleet/capex numbers were less precise and somewhat inconsistent, and the Haldiram answers were repetitive.
key_quotes: Revenue grow 6% on year in Q1 while PAT grow by nearly 30% for us. Important point is that profitability has grown much faster than revenue.

We are looking at growth only through new customers. We are not only looking at growth through new customer, we are also working closely with our existing customers to identify additional requirements across geographies and business segments.
So, around 7% to 8% growth will come with the new business and around 8%-10% growth will come through existing customers through new contract, expansion of our business.
So, these are FMCG and companies, and the festive season is coming up—Ganesh Chaturthi, followed by Dussehra, Diwali, and Durga Puja.

The rights issue will help us to strengthen our working capital position and support our growing business requirement. However, it is difficult to give a specific revenue or PAT number only against the rights issue proceed
